pull_request.title: Tracker: Prototype long-strip barrel structural staves, anchors and routes
pull_request.head: codex/long-strip-barrel
pull_request.body:
The long-strip barrel now has a continuous cooled structural sandwich between its two stereo sensors: the core and CFRP skins ARE the stave. This isolated DES-022 prototype adds the mounting/load calculation and cable/cooling routes requested in this task. It is stacked on PR #51; the separately reviewed endcap PR #53 has since been merged into this branch. Production geometry and design approval are unchanged.

- Two barrel layers at840/1060mm,86/108 staves,36 pairs/stave;6984 paired modules/13968 true1D sensor faces. Physical ±20mrad stereo,1200 strips/face;6.7/9.7mm separations include the full cooled sandwich. Both faces of the same module are required for coverage.
- **Recommend17 support stations per stave**,163.75mm spacing, two potted fasteners at each station. Conservative minimum15:14 stations exceed the40µm gravity allocation. Full1.8004kg attached load, E70GPa/G5MPa/2×gravity gives25.95µm bending+shear+overhang; independent multispan Timoshenko mesh gives23.46µm. Another10µm is allocated to joints. Moduli, keyed webs, sliding joints, rings, torsion and thermal/dynamic response need qualification.
- Two nine-pair U circuits and two12-pair harnesses per half-stave; buried tubes with explicit contained core cuts, separate face buses, end boards and collector. Conductor-sized6mm LV/HV and3.6mm48-fibre cable hypothesis conserves constituent material, checks voltage drop and keeps r1144–1169mm services fixed. Warm return-drop and oversized CMS cable controls fail and remain visible.
-36 rows/32mm phi overlap reserve follow exact helix/stereo parallax.28-row and20mm-margin failed controls are retained. This more than doubles paired modules relative to DES-011: a substantial material/channel cost. Finite coverage retains end misses; native/software PASS is not hermeticity or engineering acceptance.

Actual validation: eight model controls, native DD4hep/ROOT construction and full mass/transform/true1D ID audits, **zero overlaps at1e-5mm**,105 material/navigation rays, fresh ROOT persistence, and seeded Geant4 saved hits (eight, complete pairs in both layers).77760 vacuum tracks and164 independent oracle comparisons. ACTS conversion and calibrated response were not run.

[Design](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2c6567871ae0117b6a8a0a6484f0cebb0f2f5dee/docs/design/DES-022-long-strip-barrel.md) · [actual results/limits](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2c6567871ae0117b6a8a0a6484f0cebb0f2f5dee/docs/validation/DES-022/results.md) · [reproduction and hashes](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2c6567871ae0117b6a8a0a6484f0cebb0f2f5dee/docs/validation/DES-022/reproducibility.json)

**PR #52 review addition — x-y barrel and mounting view.** The new figure shows both barrel layers, three adjacent shingled staves, and the sensor-sandwich connection through a potted Ti fastener, epoxy joint/Ti clamp and CFRP tangent shoe/web to the bearing ring. It is an equal-scale section at z166.50 mm, within the station centred at163.75 mm, intersecting one of its two bolts. Buried cooling legs and the opposite bus/hybrid edge are visible. It reads the unchanged retained geometry inventory; the companion caption preserves the exact design-document hash pinned by the endcap. No new geometry or native-validation claim is made.

![Long-strip barrel x-y section and module mounting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/2ed5f9c8a1ca04275b6d29bd3c5a5a39b67c4eec/docs/design/figures/DES-022-barrel-xy.png)

[Figure and mounting caption](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/5d0272f72b0e0e6518f22dcdc8d52f8423196d8b/docs/validation/DES-022/xy-view.md) · [Vector x-y drawing](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2ed5f9c8a1ca04275b6d29bd3c5a5a39b67c4eec/docs/design/figures/DES-022-barrel-xy.svg) · [drawing source/provenance](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2ed5f9c8a1ca04275b6d29bd3c5a5a39b67c4eec/docs/validation/DES-022/xy-drawing.json)

![Structural stave, sandwich and routes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/2c6567871ae0117b6a8a0a6484f0cebb0f2f5dee/docs/design/figures/DES-022-stave.png)
![Anchor count and static deflection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/2c6567871ae0117b6a8a0a6484f0cebb0f2f5dee/docs/design/figures/DES-022-anchors.png)

DES-022 remains DRAFT. The canonical shared session journal covers the original barrel/endcap task once; its counters remain unrecorded. This drawing response has a separate bounded session record. Final counters for the active review turn are unavailable, so no estimate or partial usage has been imported.

events.text:
Marvelous, go ahead with the long strips, again split in barrel and end cap PRs.

The material between the sandwich sensors should not only act as the cooling and local mount, it is of course also the stave itself (design a structure how they are fixed and determine for the barrel how many anchor points are needed to prevent sagging). 

Cable and cooling routing should also be defined.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: I’ll develop the long-strip barrel and endcap in separate PRs. I’ll treat the sandwich core as the load-bearing stave, size the barrel’s support spacing against sag, and define the mounting, cooling and cable routes before building the prototypes.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: I’m using the acts-spack skill to verify the local DD4hep and Geant4 environment. The long-strip study uses two separately read out stereo sensors; I’ll retain that measurement model and replace the provisional support space with an explicit structural sandwich, mounting seats and routed services.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The Spack preflight reports changed setup and lockfile fingerprints, so I’ll verify the installed runtime directly before using it. There’s also a mechanical conflict to resolve: the old 5 mm sensor separation cannot hold the full cooled CFRP sandwich. I’ll document the required separation and calculate support spacing from bending, core shear and the complete stave load.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The selected long-strip baseline has two barrel layers at 840 and 1060 mm, and six discs per end at radii 786–1108 mm. I’m preserving those as the comparison envelope. The new model will use a continuous cooled sandwich between the sensors, with outward lifts where modules overlap, and paired mounting contacts to resist stave twist.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The first structural calculation is dominated by core shear, so a bending-only estimate would understate sag. With the full stave load, a 5 MPa core shear modulus and twice nominal gravity, the current proposal recommends 17 support stations at 163.75 mm spacing. I’ll now check the mounting webs, paired sensors and services in the native geometry.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The paired-plane coverage check found why the inherited row spacing is insufficient: oblique 1 GeV tracks can cross one sensor but miss its partner. I’m increasing the overlap using the stereo separation and worst incidence angle as the design basis, while retaining the failed layout as a control. The routing ledger also shows that the fixed 25 mm trunk fails the adverse packing scenario.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The revised layout greatly reduces the sampled pair misses, though some remain and will stay visible in the report. The native overlap check is taking too long with every component in one flat assembly. I’m grouping components by stave so the same geometry and overlap tolerance can be checked efficiently.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The grouped native check now runs successfully. It found a real clearance problem: the mounting webs cross neighbouring cores. I’m moving them to the free shingle edge and moving the buses and hybrids to the opposite edge. I’ll also distinguish the oversized cable benchmark from a conductor-sized routing proposal, with voltage-drop and warm-resistivity checks.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The corrected barrel geometry has passed the native check with zero overlaps, and Geant4 saved complete stereo-pair hits in both layers. The conservative support screen calls for at least 15 stations; I recommend 17 to leave margin for the declared modulus and load assumptions. I’m completing an independent multispan beam calculation, then proceeding to the separate endcap design.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: [Barrel PR #52](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/52) is open. For the endcap, I’m developing four rings of stereo pairs on continuous cooled petal carriers. The inner mounting region is tight against the short-strip service trunk, so I’ll keep the full model outside that corridor. I’ll also compare the shifted first disc against the original datum to show any coverage loss.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The barrel PR is open with 17 support stations per stave. The first endcap check found collisions between neighbouring electronics and between the internal webs and cable collectors. I’m correcting those passive components before repeating the geometry checks; the sensor layout stays fixed.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The proposed endcap has four rings on 12 cooled structural petals per disc, with one inner and two outer mounting contacts per petal. The gravity screen supports the installed orientation, but horizontal handling needs a temporary frame. The combined barrel/endcap services fit the reference packing case; the case with reduced space and added spare capacity still fails within the fixed corridor.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The endcap now passes the overlap and ROOT persistence checks. A routing review also showed that three cooling loops leave long heat paths near the petal edges. I’m increasing this to six distributed U-loops per petal and assigning each complete sensor pair to its nearest loop, then checking the additional service load.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The revised sensors and services clear the geometry check at 10⁻⁵ mm. The coverage study also finds tracks lost by moving the first disc to clear the barrel collector; those losses will be shown in the PR. The thermal screens remain inconclusive: they span from a small through-thickness temperature rise to a failing lateral heat-path estimate, so cooling still needs simulation and qualification.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: Both endcap Geant4 runs passed: each signed end saved both sensor faces of the same module in all six discs. I’m preparing the separate endcap PR with the drawings, routes and validation receipts. It will retain the first-disc coverage losses, handling and thermal failures, and service-packing limits for review.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The designs and local checks are complete, and I’m publishing the endcap PR stacked on the barrel PR. The barrel recommendation is 17 stations per stave with two fasteners at each station. The endcap will include the three-contact mounting concept and six-loop routing, with coverage, thermal and handling limitations called out.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: [Endcap PR #53](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/53) is now open, stacked on [barrel PR #52](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/52). Both include TDR-style drawings and retained validation evidence. I’m checking hosted CI and synchronizing the shared journal; this active turn’s final token counters are still unavailable.

events.text: Final review caught a problem in the bus model: the copper foil had insulation on only one face. I’m adding a full dielectric wrap, keeping the connection between the spine and collector, and rerunning the passive-material and transport checks before closing out.

events.text: The fully wrapped bus model passes the fresh geometry, persistence and Geant4 checks. Its added material is included in the revised 1.497 kg petal load. The barrel’s hosted build has passed; I’m finishing the endcap closeout and hosted validation.

coverage.responses: Public responses and recorded outcomes; no private model state or hidden reasoning.
coverage.token_accounting: References only. Never sum accounts across PRs or assign a shared turn by text length.
coverage.unknowns: Unrecorded names, models, tools, subagent identities and response links remain unknown; empty lists are not zero activity.
coverage.remote: Snapshot, not live synchronization; deleted/edited history and emoji reactions are not recovered.
coverage.branch_only: Pinned branch journal snapshots are references, not imported counters. Unretained or other-device inputs remain unknown.
